title: Sidecar adapter for resilient trace context & lightweight telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Across our fleet we see fragmented trace header formats, noop fallbacks when a framework tears async contexts, and high variance in tail latency for trace-enriched requests. SDK-only changes are fragile because some customers run language runtimes, edge proxies, or sidecars that rewrite headers.

Goal: Build a small, language-agnostic local adapter (agent/sidecar) pattern plus lightweight SDK hooks that together provide:
- deterministic trace header normalization (W3C traceparent, b3, legacy vendor headers)
- request-level sampling decisions surfaced consistently to downstream services
- a resilient path for telemetry emission that survives async-context loss (local UDP/gRPC buffer + bounded retry)
- a minimal API for SDKs and middleware to attach span metadata without requiring deep framework integration

Scope:
- Sidecar binary (Go) that runs per host/container and listens on localhost:4318 (configurable) for a compact HTTP/gRPC shim used by SDKs and proxies.
- Header normalizer: inbound/outbound rewrite rules, header precedence table, and a compatibility mode to preserve legacy headers for 7 days after rollout.
- Sampling proxy: centralize sampling decisions when available, otherwise enforce local deterministic sampling using trace-id hashing.
- SDK hooks: tiny client libraries (Node, Python, Java) that call the sidecar to create spans/annotations and return a local span handle. Hooks degrade to no-op quickly if sidecar dead.
- Exporter shim: sidecar buffers spans and forwards to our OTLP collector with batching and backoff.

Non-goals: full OpenTelemetry SDK replacement, heavy in-process instrumentation, multi-host cross-process trace reconstruction (collector job handles that later).

Success metrics:
- Reduction in trace-coverage gaps for async frameworks by >=80% in canary services.
- 50% drop in customer tickets citing missing trace context or header mangling.
- CPU overhead of sidecar <1% of service baseline under typical load.

Design tradeoffs:
- Local sidecar increases surface area (deployment/ops) but avoids language-specific runtime shims and reduces per-language complexity.
- Deterministic local sampling guarantees consistent decision without cross-service latency but can skew sampling distribution; we will add a coordination mode for Dedicated customers.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement sidecar + Node/Python SDK hooks, run internal canary on infra-team services (2 weeks).
2) Enable header normalization in passive mode (log diffs) for two weeks.
3) Active enforcement + deterministic sampling for canary subset.
4) Expand to customer-facing gateways and provide helm chart for Dedicated/Private installs.

Operational concerns:
- Sidecar crash loops must not affect application process; SDK fallback must be robust.
- Backpressure: bounded queue + shed oldest when queue saturated; emit metric when sheds happen.
- Security: sidecar exposes only localhost by default; mTLS for Dedicated installs; security review flagged (see security_review_required).

comments: 2026-02-16 - Initial scoping and tech spike completed. PoC sidecar (Go) can accept compact HTTP span writes and forward to OTLP. Node hook implemented as 8-line wrapper. Next: add header normalization rules and sampling proxy.

2026-02-22 - Design review with infra and security. Decided to default to localhost-only and require explicit opt-in for cluster-wide binding. Security asked for KCV of headers stored in sidecar logs; we'll redact by default.

2026-03-01 - Benchmarks on canary service: sidecar adds ~0.6% CPU at 2k RPS with 128B average payload. Deterministic sampling logic adds negligible CPU. Added metric trace.sidecar.queue_drop when queue > 1000.

2026-03-04 - PR 4831 opened for minimal shim. Requesting review from @Marcus Chen for Node ergonomics and @Elena Rossi for header normalization rules. Linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4831

2026-03-07 - Review feedback: Marcus requested graceful-sync API to wait for span flush on process exit; implemented in SDK v0.3. Elena suggested precedence table: OT-Trace > W3C > B3 > vendor. Updated design doc.

2026-03-10 - Canary rollout started for infra-service-1 and gateway-dev. Passive header normalization logging enabled. Monitoring dashboards created: observability/sidecar/trace-coverage and observability/sidecar/queue-sheds. Next: enable active enforcement in one region after 72h of stability.
